description.narrative:
Southeast Asia is one of the largest global supplier markets for mineral raw materials; accounting for about US$250 billion in 2018. In recent years, the aspirations of governments to achieve the target of net zero emissions by 2050 has led them to heighten their focus on sourcing critical minerals. They have forged ahead with various mining projects: involving upstream and/or downstream operations. While the green energy agenda is aimed at mitigating climate change risks, the transition from petroleum to alternative energy using green technologies, that demand critical minerals, has had serious environmental impacts. This has highlighted the need for wider stakeholder participation, particularly affected communities in mineral-rich resource nations to ensure the goal of a just and sustainable transition. This project enable CANSEA to undertake critical Mineral study with the following objectives:
a) Build on the findings and insights from existing studies and reports on current trends and concerns with critical minerals’ mining, on environmental and human rights issues; and b) Extrapolate the findings to determine the common gaps in national policies and impedimentsto a Just and Sustainable Transition in the region, particularly in Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, and Vietnam, with reference to critical minerals mining.
The project Activities includes:
a) Mapping of different groups working on Critical Minerals in Southeast Asia b) Consultation with Oxfam-CANSEA JET Regional Partnership and Network to present work-in-progress and get their inputs prior to completion of study. c) Development of strategy on how report can be used by CSOs for advocacy with ASEAN.

participating-org.narrative:
The Climate Action Network Southeast Asia Sdn Bhd (CANSEA) was established in January 1992 but formerly the idea of forming the regional network was raised when WALHI of Indonesia, EPSM of Malaysia and Green Forum – Haribon Foundation of the Philippines were invited as observers to the Second INS Session in June 1991 in Geneva. It was felt that this form of partnership was needed to address the socio-political issues associated with the climate change debate and to exchange information, strengthen communicationand coordinate activities at the regional level. This initiative further strengthened the regions link up with Climate Action Network (CAN) in Africa, South Asia, United States, Europe, Latin America, Eastern Europe, United Kingdom and the Pacific.
TheCANSEA regional network is designed to create synergy in the matter of doing advocacy work at the local and national levels with our respective governments and internationally to join forces with the rest of CAN bringing along the sentiments and concernsof the developing countries, particularly the Southeast Asian perspective, to the lobbying/negotiating arena (the UN Climate Conference of Parties with all its subsidiary bodies meetings [SBSTA, SBI]). See more information about CANSEA via its website www.cansea.net. CANSEA’s relationship with Oxfam happened recently in 2022. Following a series of engagements, Oxfam agreed to support CANSEA host a series of Regional Meetingsfrom August 23-26. During these landmark meetings, a CANSEA Just Transition Strategy for Asia was developed in consultation with members and representatives of CAN in SEA, South Asia, Pacific Islands. Also participating in these discussions were CANSEA’s allies and partners actively involved in Just Transition work like Oxfam, Stockholm Environment Institute and Friedrich Ebert Stiftung. Soon after, Oxfam developed its Influencing JET strategy document for Asia. Another related development that took place three months later was the adoption of a work program on Just Transition atthe conclusion of COP27 of the UNFCCC on November 19. The Sharm el-Sheikh Implementation Plan asserts that Just Transition is founded on Social Dialogue. As Parties to the decision, governments worldwide,including those in SEA, are obligated to mainstream Just Transition.
This leads to building an interest and understanding of CANSEA to initiate a project idea to support an implementation of Oxfam I-JET project.
In this regard, CANSEA initiate a project idea with objective to raising awareness of Just Transition in Three Countries in Southeast Asia with the following project deliverables:
• Baselines and scoping study reports that contain thematic reports such as: (1) report on demography and political economy of the areas identified for community engagement;(2) Reports on community-based renewable energy models; (3) Mapping of Just Transition activities being carried out by other parties; and (4) record of communications on the project through CANSEA’s social media channels. • A logframe for implementing Just Transition over the next four years.
